Work · Sustainability & social systems

Organisations, institutions and sustainability as a systems problem

What determines whether organisations commit to sustainable development and circular-economy principles?

Status
Published
Period
2023 – present
Role
Co-author; research associate
Where
Political Economy of Sustainable Development Lab, University of Athens
SDSN Youth Greece
With
Antonios Alevizos, Christianna Vrouvaki, Andreas Papandreou
Methods
  • Systems frameworks
  • Institutional analysis
  • Survey analysis
  • Data visualisation
Links
SDG4U project team

Question

Sustainability targets are set for organisations, but organisations are themselves systems of people, routines and external pressures. The question is which of those internal and external forces determine whether an organisation actually commits to sustainable development and circular-economy principles.

System

Non-governmental organisations in Greece, studied through the lenses of organisational culture, institutional isomorphism (the pressures that make organisations resemble one another) and systems frameworks that treat the organisation and its environment as coupled.

Result

The analysis was published in 2026 in Circular Economy and Sustainability (Alevizos, Kaminas, Vrouvaki & Papandreou), open access under CC BY 4.0.

Related work

As a research associate at the Political Economy of Sustainable Development Lab (University of Athens, since 2025) I work on climate-change reporting, data visualisation and scientific storytelling. At SDSN Youth Greece I coordinate the network’s collaborations and projects on the Sustainable Development Goals (network coordinator since 2025; sustainability research fellow 2023–2025), and I contributed research, writing and dissemination to SDG4U, an EU-funded higher-education project on Sustainable Development Goal 4 (2024–2025).

Status

One peer-reviewed article published (2026). Other activities are ongoing and are policy and outreach work rather than research outputs.
